direct_answer:
TotalEnergies integrates sustainability-related performance into incentive/remuneration schemes through (i) annual variable compensation and (ii) a performance share plan, using a mix of financial and extra-financial (sustainability-related) criteria. For the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the variable portion is assessed against quantifiable targets including Safety and GHG emissions change parameters (Scope 1+2 from operated facilities) as well as qualitative criteria (personal contribution); extra-financial criteria represent 39% of the maximum annual variable portion and cover items such as safety performance, GHG reduction, supervision of the transition strategy, profitability of renewables, and CSR performance [Source 5][Source 1]. For senior executives, extra-financial criteria represent 30% of annual variable compensation and include safety, GHG reduction and carbon intensity, diversity, and individual performance (with weightings adapted by role) [Source 1].

In the performance share plan (covering the Chairman/CEO and eligible employees), extra-financial criteria represent 30% of performance conditions; for the 2024 grant, climate-linked award criteria account for 30% (15% linked to lifecycle carbon intensity of energy products sold to customers and 15% linked to changes in methane emissions) [Source 5][Source 1].

Governance/approval: the Board of Directors decided to include a quantifiable GHG-emissions-change criterion in the CEO’s variable compensation starting in 2019 and reviews the CEO compensation policy annually, on the recommendation of the Compensation Committee [Source 5].
compliance_rationale: The passages provide key characteristics of the schemes (annual variable compensation and performance share plan), identify specific sustainability targets/metrics used (safety; GHG emissions change Scope 1+2; carbon intensity; methane emissions; diversity; CSR/HSE; transition strategy; renewables profitability), and quantify the proportion of variable remuneration/performance conditions linked to extra-financial or climate criteria (39% for CEO annual variable; 30% for senior executives annual variable; 30% extra-financial in performance share plan; and a detailed 30% climate split for the 2024 performance share plan) [Source 5][Source 1]. They also state that the Board of Directors reviews the CEO compensation policy annually (on Compensation Committee recommendation) and that the Board decided on inclusion of GHG criteria starting in 2019 [Source 5]. However, the evidence does not fully cover approval/update levels and sustainability-linked remuneration details for the supervisory body/directors’ remuneration policy beyond a cross-reference, nor does it explicitly state the proportion of variable remuneration dependent on sustainability targets for directors (as distinct from the CEO) [Source 5].
disclosure_gaps: Explicit sustainability-linked incentive/remuneration details for members of the administrative/supervisory body other than the Chairman/CEO (e.g., directors), beyond a reference to another section not provided in the retrieved passages [Source 5].

Clear statement of the level(s) in the undertaking at which the terms of all relevant incentive schemes (not only the CEO policy) are approved and updated (e.g., for senior executives and the broader performance share plan) [Source 5][Source 1].

Explicit mapping of which sustainability-related metrics are used as formal performance benchmarks in remuneration policies for each body (administrative/management/supervisory), versus being described as criteria, for all relevant roles [Source 1][Source 5].
key_findings: CEO annual variable compensation includes quantifiable sustainability targets (Safety and GHG emissions change Scope 1+2 from operated facilities) and qualitative criteria; extra-financial criteria represent 39% of the maximum variable portion [Source 5].
CEO annual variable compensation extra-financial criteria include safety performance, GHG reduction, supervision of transition strategy, profitability of renewables, and CSR performance [Source 1].

Senior executives’ annual variable compensation includes extra-financial criteria representing 30%, including safety, GHG reduction and carbon intensity, diversity, and individual performance [Source 1].

Performance share plan includes 30% extra-financial performance conditions; for the 2024 grant, 30% is tied to climate objectives split between lifecycle carbon intensity (15%) and methane emissions changes (15%) [Source 5][Source 1].

Board governance: Board decided to add a quantifiable GHG criterion to CEO variable pay starting in 2019; CEO compensation policy is reviewed annually by the Board on Compensation Committee recommendation [Source 5].
